_note: PLAN.md 8.2b's TRADE corner button, made real. The market page is the one of
the four that is a mechanism rather than a wireframe, so it needs numbers, and
the numbers belong here rather than inside the two commands that spend them:
these are balance figures the project owner will want to move without reading
GDScript.
EVERY VALUE IS AN INTEGER, and that is a hard constraint rather than a style
choice. `TributeCommand` and `MarketExchangeCommand` run inside the sim, whose
arithmetic must be bit-identical on an ARM phone and an x86 desktop (PLAN.md
5). A tax of `0.1` would be a float in the middle of a state transition; a tax
of `10` percent is a multiply and an integer divide, which cannot drift. Same
reason ages.json counts advancement in ticks and not in seconds.
GOLD IS THE CURRENCY, which is why it has no exchange entry: the market buys
and sells food, wood and stone FOR gold. That is Age of Empires' model and it
is the reason gold is worth mining at all -- a market that traded any resource
for any other would make three of the four interchangeable and the fourth
pointless.
`building` IS THE PRECONDITION FOR BOTH HALVES. Trading is something a market
lets you do, the way training is something a barracks lets you do -- and it is
declared here rather than written into the two commands so the two cannot end
up gated on different buildings, or on nothing. It is also how the age gate is
inherited for free: `building.market` is age 2 in buildings.json, so requiring
the building requires the age without stating it twice.
THE SPREAD IS THE WHOLE COST OF TRADING. Buy at 130 gold a hundred, sell at
70: a round trip loses 60% of what it moved, so the market is an emergency
valve for a shortage and never a substitute for gathering. AoE2's market opens
at 100/100 and DRIFTS with every trade, which is a better mechanism and is
deliberately not this one -- a drifting price is per-player mutable state, so
it would have to live on SimPlayer, ride the snapshot and enter
`state_hash()`. Worth doing when the market has been played with; not worth
guessing at now. Fixed prices are one data change away from being the
starting point of that.
TRIBUTE'S TAX is 10%, matching the mockup the project owner drew
(UI_Design_Market). AoE2 charges 30% until Coinage removes it; 10% with no
tech to remove it is the same idea at a tenth the sting, and it exists at all
so that shuffling resources between allies is not free -- otherwise two
players are one economy with two build queues.
`increment` is what one press of a Tribute button sends. 100 rather than 10,
because a button that moves a tenth of a villager-load is a button somebody
has to press forty times.
